1000.title: THelpViewer
content: [b]THelpViewer context-sensitive help[/b]
Press F1 in the viewer to open help for the active tool or game. In DOS
Prompt, F1 goes to the emulated program instead; request this
application help from the DOS Prompt menu.
Links, long articles and fixed-width tables use the same UHF 2.0 model
as converted DOS HELP files. Use the scrollbar or mouse wheel when an
article is taller than its window.
│ Key              │ Action                                     │
│ F1               │ Context help                               │
│ F10              │ Activate the menu bar                      │
│ F5               │ Zoom or restore the active window          │
│ F6 / Shift-F6    │ Select next or previous window             │
│ Alt-F3           │ Close the active window                    │
[link:topic=2090]Clipboard[/link]: Ctrl+Ins copies, Shift+Del cuts, Shift+Ins pastes.
Use Cmd+C/X/V on macOS or Ctrl+C/X/V on Windows/Linux too.

Choose a topic link above, browse Contents or use Help > Index to find a
named feature. Each game's own article explains its rules, controls and
score conditions rather than only naming the game.

1100.title: System menu
content: The system menu opens small utilities, the Widget Gallery and screen
savers without replacing your open HELP windows. Use it to inspect the
runtime, calculate a value or look up a character while keeping your
place in a reference.
Signed-in users find Colors and theme settings under their user menu >
Configuration; guests can use the system menu. About is available under
Help. F10 activates the menu bar, and Escape leaves a menu without
choosing a command.

1200.title: HELP files
content: Help Files browses the server's generated HELP catalog. Open displays a
selected HELP or Docs file; it does not install software. Administrators
install or remove HELP editions separately through Configuration > HELP
Packages.
Products group verified editions in natural version order. A one-file
edition opens directly, while editions with several files offer a
submenu. When a product has only one file, its menu item includes the
version without an extra submenu. A tool's own version may differ from
its compiler release.
Cross-file links keep the original source filename and open a companion
when its bundle exists in the catalog. An unavailable target produces an
explanation rather than silently replacing the link with unrelated
content.

1300.title: Documents
content: Documents displays Markdown documentation in a read-only Editor-style
window with a blue background and yellow base text. Headings, code
examples, tables and links remain part of the same document window.
Use the scrollbars or mouse wheel to read longer pages; a wide table can
require horizontal scrolling. Ctrl-F opens Find for the active document,
and Ctrl-L repeats its current search.
Select text and use Copy to place it on the system clipboard. This view
is read-only: Cut and Paste cannot change the document stored on the
server.

1400.title: Search
content: [b]Choosing where to search[/b]
Choose Search all HELP/Docs for server-wide full-text or topic search,
or Find in active window for the currently open HELP or document. Only
available scopes are enabled, and the radio buttons select one scope at
a time. Find Again repeats the active window's current query.
Search Topics lists matching topics together with their source. The line
below the list shows the original HELP file's long title, helping
distinguish similarly named entries from different products.
[b]Global index progress[/b]
The server maintains a persistent index when published HELP or Docs
change. During a build, ▤ and a percentage appear beside Downloads and
the clock; clicking the indicator reopens Building Global Index after
Hide. Hiding its dialog does not stop indexing.
HELP download, extraction, conversion and publication pause the index.
The indicator becomes ▤ ‖ and the progress window says Waiting for HELP
processing. It resumes against the final published library after HELP
work ends, including failures and Retry; DOS- or MIDI-only work does not
hold it.
[b]Recovery and skipped files[/b]
Jobs and per-source progress survive a server restart. Committed,
unchanged sources are skipped, while an interrupted source is repeated.
Completed data stays searchable during updates.
Unreadable files are reported as skipped without hiding results from
other sources. Unchanged corrupt-file failures remain recorded across
restarts; changing the source's content or permissions makes it eligible
for another attempt.

1500.title: Games
content: Open a game from the Games menu and use F1 while its window is active to
read that game's rules and controls. Timer-based games use
inactive-window pause handling, so changing windows does not require
racing a background board.
[b]Hall of Fame[/b]
The [H] title control opens the game's ten-entry Hall of Fame. Rankings
use the appropriate measure: some games reward more points, while
puzzles reward fewer moves or turns. Sokoban compares the level reached
before its move count.
Where available, scores are read from and saved to the server. A local
browser fallback is used when the server cannot be reached. A qualifying
result can ask for a player name; opening [H] only displays the
rankings.
See the individual topics for legal moves, ending conditions, shortcuts
and score rules. Starting a new game can discard an unfinished board;
the Hall of Fame is not a saved-game browser.

1600.title: Windows
content: Tile, Cascade and Window List help organise open HELP files, documents,
tools and games. Tile arranges windows side by side, while Cascade
overlaps them with their title bars visible; Window List selects an
existing window without reopening its file.
F5 zooms or restores the active target. F6 and Shift-F6 cycle windows,
and Alt-F3 closes the active one. Drag a title bar to move a window;
growable windows also have a lower-right size control.
Window frames and title controls are shared TVFrame/TVWindow objects.
Inactive frames indicate which window will receive input; bring a window
forward before using its contents.

1700.title: Context Help
content: F1 opens context-sensitive help for the current action instead of always
returning to the same introduction. The active menu item has first
priority, followed by the focused view, the active managed window or
dialog, and finally the application context.
Each view supplies a Turbo Vision-style hc... number, which selects a
topic in THELPVIEWER.HLP. The application stores that help as the same
UHF 2.0 JSON model used for converted HELP files.
Use the Help menu or status line for Back, Contents and Index. Links
jump to related topics in the existing help viewer, and the normal
scrollbars handle long articles and fixed-width tables.

2000.title: About
content: About shows the running application version and author credits. The
version is read from package metadata, not from a hard-coded label, so
it identifies the server build you are currently using.
When reporting a problem, include that version and the affected file,
topic or tool. About is available from the Help menu; closing it returns
to the previously active window without changing your workspace.

2010.title: Open a File
content: Open a File selects a HELP or Docs file from the generated catalog.
Browse the virtual directories and two-column file list, or begin typing
in the focused filename input; Enter opens the selected file, and
double-clicking a directory enters it.
The ▐↓▌ control opens recent files. Its History window has a close
control and can also be dismissed with Escape or a click outside.
Selecting a history entry fills the associated input without creating a
second file catalog.
Cancel or the frame close control leaves the current file unopened.
Package installation belongs to the administrator's HELP Packages
dialog, not to this file chooser.

2020.title: Change Directory
content: Change Directory navigates the virtual HELP and Docs folders used by
Open a File. It changes the chooser's current location, not the server's
host filesystem or a DOS Prompt drive.
Select a directory in the list or enter a path, then use Chdir to apply
it. Revert restores the initial path, while Cancel closes the dialog
without applying a new location.
The history control shares the History window used by Open a File and
Find. Mouse wheel and scrollbars move a long directory list; Escape
dismisses an open history before leaving the dialog.

2030.title: Find
content: Find searches either all indexed HELP/Docs on the server or the active
HELP/document window. Choose one available scope with the radio buttons;
a disabled option means that target is currently unavailable.
The first input is focused so you can type immediately. Alt-F activates
the Find label and focuses its linked input again. Enter the text and
use Find; Find Again repeats the active window's existing query.
The arrow beside the input opens previous queries. Select an entry to
reuse it, or dismiss history with Escape, its close control or the arrow
again. Closing Find does not modify the source HELP or document.

2040.title: Colors
content: Colors edits the DOS foreground/background attributes used by the
interface. Choose a Group and Item, then select foreground and
background colours; the preview lets you check whether text remains
readable.
Default restores only the selected item's standard value, while Reset
All restores the complete Turbo Vision palette. OK keeps the chosen
palette, and Cancel or closing the dialog restores the palette from
before editing.
Ordinary users can edit colours too. Signed-in users open Colors from
their user menu > Configuration; guests use the system menu. Settings
are saved in this browser and are not synchronised between accounts or
devices.

2050.title: Widget Gallery
content: Widget Gallery demonstrates the shared Turbo Vision controls used
throughout the application. It is a testing area for labels, inputs,
lists, checkboxes, radio buttons, multi-state clusters, disabled states
and command buttons.
Use Tab and Shift-Tab to move focus, activate label mnemonics to reach
linked controls, and use arrows or the mouse to change a list selection.
Space toggles a checkbox; radio buttons choose one value from their
group.
The Event log records interactions so you can compare what was selected
with the command received. Clear log empties that display, while Message
opens a standard MessageBox. Disabled examples are deliberately
unavailable and should not react to clicks.
The gallery does not edit HELP files, install packages or change server
accounts. It exercises the same shared controls, focus rules and
palettes as the real dialogs.

2060.title: CD/MIDI Player
content: [b]Playing and choosing music[/b]
The CD/MIDI Player plays game music through a SoundFont synthesizer.
Choose a track and use Play, Pause or Stop; Pause retains the playback
position, while Stop resets it. Previous and Next change tracks, and
clicking the progress bar seeks within the current song.
Cover art appears when the configured source supplies it. The first use
may need time to prepare the synthesizer and download its SoundFont; the
browser can also require a user gesture before allowing sound.
[b]More, Filter and automatic next track[/b]
More expands the window to reveal the track list, Filter with history,
and Random next track. Type part of a title to narrow a large catalog,
or use the filter's history arrow to reuse an earlier value.
A finished song starts the next track in order unless Random next track
is checked. Selecting a different track changes the requested music, its
title and its available cover together.
[b]Downloads and incomplete albums[/b]
A cloud at a row's end means the track has not been downloaded. Playing
it sends a priority request to the front of the shared queue; it can
download during HELP/DOS work, and repeated requests do not start
duplicate transfers.
The requested song starts when its download is ready, even if another
album has failed. Stop or Pause cancels waiting to play, not the shared
download. Closing the player also cancels that automatic start. A failed
song shows its error; use Play or Downloads to retry.
After restart, only missing tracks or incomplete albums enter Downloads.
Complete albums and cached source indexes do not flash Downloading or
reset progress; successful entries stay in Completed downloads.
The Downloads menu beside the clock shows shared packages and MIDI
albums without opening another automatic MIDI progress window. Closing
that menu does not stop downloading, and ZIP track totals can grow as
archive members are discovered.
A partial library keeps playable tracks and reports its download-error
count. Valid tracks and covers survive rejected members in the same ZIP,
while text renamed .mid is rejected and an incomplete album remains
failed and retryable. Check Downloads for the failed album or member.
[b]Formats, statistics and administration[/b]
Standard MIDI, RIFF/RMID and counted DOS MIDI are decoded for playback.
Statistics count plays and active listening time, excluding pauses;
downloaded tracks, covers and the catalog are cached under var/midi.
Administrators choose server providers and albums in Configuration >
MIDI Sources and can rebuild the library from midi-sources.json.
Rebuilding is separate from the player's transport controls.

2070.title: HELP viewer
content: HELP viewer opens converted references in the shared help window. Use
links to jump to topics or companion files, and use Back, Index,
Contents and Search from the menu or status line without a second
navigation strip inside the window.
UHF 2.0 keeps source-defined colours, styles and fixed-width text.
Native TextScreens retain their original glyphs, palette and embedded
fonts; blink attributes remain available, while reduced motion keeps
blinking glyphs visible.
A native alias resolves to its real topic. Missing destinations produce
a Help Error and leave the current article in place, rather than
guessing another topic or silently dropping the link.
Previous and Next follow a topic's defined continuation and are
available only when another page exists. In multi-page Sidekick help,
More.. continues the article, while Content lets you choose Page 2, Page
3 and later pages directly. A file without an alphabetical index opens
its available Contents before falling back to a topic.

2080.title: Document viewer
content: The document viewer uses a read-only Editor palette for Markdown pages.
The lower-left RO indicator means read-only, and its line/column values
describe the editor's current position rather than a saved editing
cursor.
Scroll through the document, follow its links and use Find to locate
text. Select text and press Ctrl+Ins or your system's Copy shortcut to
use it elsewhere.
Cut and Paste cannot replace this document's contents. Opening
documentation does not create a writable editor or save changes back to
the server.

2090.title: Dialogs
content: Dialogs group related controls such as text inputs, lists, checkboxes
and command buttons. Tab and Shift-Tab move focus, Enter activates the
default button, and Escape closes the dialog unless its active control
reserves Escape for an operation of its own.
Clicking outside a dialog never closes it. A modal dialog blocks
background input until it is dismissed; a nonmodal tool can remain open
while you switch to another window.
[b]System clipboard[/b]
Ctrl+Ins copies, Shift+Del cuts and Shift+Ins pastes. Native Cmd+C/X/V
on macOS and Ctrl+C/X/V on Windows/Linux also work in shared input
fields, subject to browser clipboard permissions.
Paste respects input length and validators, so a token, email or numeric
field can reject invalid text rather than silently storing it. HELP and
Docs are read-only: selected text can be copied but cannot be cut or
replaced.
If clipboard access is unavailable, use the browser's native shortcuts
or menu when requested. Clipboard text is never sent to the server or
saved as application data.

2100.title: Calendar
content: Calendar browses dates in a month grid and applies Gregorian leap-year
rules when crossing February or changing years. It is a date viewer, not
an appointment calendar; selecting a day does not create an event.
Left/Right or -/+ move one day, while Up/Down move one week. Page Up and
Page Down change the month; hold Ctrl with those keys to change the year
instead.
Home or Space returns to today's date. The visible controls also let you
browse months and years, and crossing a month boundary updates the
displayed calendar automatically.
[link:topic=2090]Dialogs and tools[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2110.title: ASCII Table
content: ASCII Chart displays the 256 byte values and their DOS CP437 glyph
presentation. Use it to identify a character, inspect box-drawing
symbols or compare a visible glyph with a byte code in a HELP format.
Click a cell to select it. Left/Right move one code at a time and
Up/Down move between chart rows; the selection wraps within the 0–255
byte range.
The report below the chart shows the selected character, decimal value
and hexadecimal value. This is a byte-oriented DOS character table, not
a list of every Unicode character or a declaration that every HELP file
uses CP437.

2120.title: Calculator
content: Calculator is a small desk calculator for addition, subtraction,
multiplication, division and percentages. Use the digit and operation
buttons or type on the keyboard; Enter performs the equals operation.
Backspace removes the last entered digit. Escape is reserved for
correcting the current entry and does not close this dialog; use C/Clear
to reset the calculation and the sign control to change a value's sign.
Calculations use the current operand and operation rather than parsing a
full expression with parentheses. A division by zero or unsupported
numeric result shows an error; Clear starts again. Close the window with
its frame control or Alt-F3 when finished.
[link:topic=2090]Dialogs and tools[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2130.title: Screen saver
content: Screen savers temporarily cover the desktop without closing its windows.
Choose Stars, Bounce, Clock, Matrix or the DOS Navigator-style Projector
from the system menu.
A mouse movement, click or key press dismisses the saver and restores
the previously focused control. This is a visual effect, not a security
lock or a request to sign out.
If automatic idle activation is enabled, a saver is selected after
inactivity. Return to the application before issuing commands; the input
that dismisses the saver is used to leave it.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=1600]Windows[/link]
[link:topic=1100]System menu[/link]

2140.title: Puzzle
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Arrange the fifteen lettered tiles A through O in reading order on the 4
x 4 board, leaving the blank in the lower-right corner. Only a tile
directly beside the blank can move; diagonal moves and jumping over
another tile are not allowed.
The starting position is scrambled through legal moves, so the puzzle is
solvable. Plan how a move changes both the chosen tile and the next
position of the blank instead of chasing one letter at a time.
[b]Controls[/b]
Click a neighbouring tile to slide it into the gap, or use the arrow
keys to move an adjacent tile in the indicated direction. A tile that
does not share an edge with the blank stays in place.
After solving the board, clicking a tile or pressing an arrow or
character key starts a new scramble. The Move counter records successful
tile moves, not clicks on tiles that cannot move.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Fewer moves rank higher in the Puzzle Hall of Fame; [H] opens the list.
Try finishing a row without disturbing completed tiles, and keep enough
space for the remaining tiles to circulate.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2150.title: Tetris
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Place falling pieces so they form complete horizontal rows. A piece can
move or rotate only while it fits inside the field and does not overlap
settled blocks. When it lands, it joins the stack and a new piece
appears.
Complete rows disappear and the blocks above fall into the space. The
game ends when the next piece cannot enter the field; keeping the stack
low gives you more time to arrange difficult shapes.
[b]Controls and setup[/b]
Left/Right move the piece and Up rotates it. Down or Space drops it
straight to its lowest legal position immediately; this is a hard drop,
not a slow-descent key. P pauses or resumes, and N starts a new game.
Setup chooses a starting level, Tetris or the extended Pentix piece set,
and whether the next-piece preview is visible. Applying those settings
starts a new board. Enter or Space starts again after game over.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Placing pieces and clearing rows earn points, with an extra bonus for an
empty field. Higher levels increase the speed. Use the next-piece
preview to reserve landing space and avoid holes underneath settled
blocks.
An inactive game window pauses the action. [H] opens the rankings for
the current Tetris/Pentix game type; more points rank higher.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2160.title: Mines
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Reveal every safe cell on a 9 x 9 board containing 10 mines. A revealed
number counts mines in the eight surrounding cells, including diagonals;
an empty cell opens its connected safe area automatically.
The first revealed cell is safe. Revealing a mine ends the game, so use
the neighbouring counts to decide which hidden cells are safe instead of
treating every unopened cell as a guess.
[b]Controls[/b]
Left-click reveals a cell, while right-click toggles a flag on a
suspected mine. With the keyboard, arrows move the cursor, Home/End
reach the first or last cell in its row, Enter or Space reveals, and F
toggles a flag.
A flagged cell is protected from being revealed until you remove its
flag. The face button starts a fresh board; flags are reminders, not
proof that a cell really contains a mine.
[b]Winning and scoring[/b]
You win by uncovering all non-mine cells; flagging every mine is not
required. The timer begins with the first reveal, pauses when the window
is inactive, and stops on a win or loss.
Winning times are ranked with shorter times first. Use [H] for the Hall
of Fame, and compare overlapping number clues before opening a risky
square.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2170.title: BreakOut
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Keep the ball in play with the paddle and destroy the bricks above it.
The ball bounces off the walls, ceiling, paddle and bricks; missing it
at the bottom costs one of your three lives.
Clearing every brick starts the next level with a new wall and a ball
waiting on the paddle. Levels become faster, and the game finishes when
no lives remain.
[b]Controls[/b]
Hold Left/Right to move the paddle; Home and Page Up provide alternative
left/right controls. Space or Up launches a waiting ball, so you can
choose the launch position before committing.
N or New starts a fresh game. After game over, Enter or Space can also
restart. The game pauses while its window or browser focus is inactive;
return to the window before steering again.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Destroyed bricks earn points, with higher rows worth more. [H] opens the
Hall of Fame, where higher scores rank first. Aim with the paddle edges
to change the ball's horizontal direction and open a route into the
upper rows.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2180.title: Sokoban
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Push every crate onto a goal square. The player can walk through free
floor cells and push one adjacent crate when the cell beyond it is free;
crates cannot be pulled, pushed through walls or pushed as a chain.
A crate can cover a goal and later be moved away again. The level is
solved only when all goals contain crates, so parking one in a non-goal
corner can make the board impossible to finish.
[b]Controls and levels[/b]
Use the arrows to walk or push. Before a level is solved, U or Undo
reverses the last move. R or Restart resets the current level. Prev/Next
browse the available levels, but changing a level resets its current
board.
After solving a level, Enter or Space advances to the next. After the
last level it starts a new campaign. The Info box shows the current
level, moves and pushes so you can compare a solution with another
attempt.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Hall of Fame compares the level reached first, then prefers fewer total
moves at the same level. A higher level outranks a lower-level result
even when its move count is larger.
Campaign ranking requires completed preceding levels; skipping
unfinished levels is not a shortcut to a qualified score. On leaving a
qualifying run, the current level and total moves can be submitted. Use
[H] to inspect the rankings.
Before pushing a crate, check that you can still reach its other side.
Work backwards from the goals and use Undo before a temporary blockage
becomes permanent.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2190.title: Lines
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Make a straight line of at least five balls of the same colour on the 9
x 9 board. Horizontal, vertical and both diagonal lines count;
completing a line removes its balls and frees their cells.
A ball may move only through a connected path of empty cells, using
horizontal and vertical steps. It cannot jump over another ball, even
when the destination itself is empty.
[b]Controls and new balls[/b]
Click a ball to select it, then click an empty destination. Clicking
another ball changes the selection. A blocked route leaves the board
unchanged, while a legal move that clears no line adds three new balls.
The Next box previews the upcoming colours. A move that completes a line
avoids that normal spawn, although newly added balls can also form and
clear lines. N or New starts another game.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Each removed ball earns two points, and the game ends when no empty
cells remain. [H] shows the Hall of Fame with higher scores first.
Keep routes open between different parts of the board and avoid filling
a nearly completed line's last accessible square with the wrong colour.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2200.title: Reversi
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Reversi is played on an 8 x 8 board. You play black against the
computer's white discs, beginning with four discs in the centre. A legal
move places a disc on an empty cell and traps at least one uninterrupted
line of white discs between it and another black disc.
Trapped discs flip to your colour. Captures may run horizontally,
vertically or diagonally, and one placement can flip lines in several
directions. A move that captures nothing is illegal.
[b]Controls and ending[/b]
Click a legal empty cell on your turn; the computer responds after its
move delay. N or New starts a fresh board. The Info box shows the turn
and both disc counts.
If one player has no legal move, that turn is passed automatically. The
game ends when neither player can move, not only when every square is
occupied; the side with more discs wins, and equal counts are a draw.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
A human win can enter the Hall of Fame using the final black-minus-white
margin, with a larger margin ranked higher. [H] displays the list.
Corners are valuable because discs placed there cannot be bracketed from
behind. Avoid giving the computer an easy corner just to gain a few
temporary discs.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2210.title: Ludo
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Move all four pieces of your colour out of base, around the common track
and into your home lane. A six brings a piece out of base, provided your
starting square is not occupied by another piece of your own.
Landing on an opponent on the common track sends that piece back to
base. You cannot finish a move on your own piece, overshoot the end of
your home lane, or pass one of your own pieces inside that lane.
A six grants another roll after a legal move. When every piece is still
in base, the player can have up to three attempts to roll a usable
result. You win when all four pieces are in the home lane; they do not
all have to reach its very last square.
[b]Controls and players[/b]
Use Roll, R or Space when it is time to throw the die. Click a legal
piece or press its number 1–4 to move it; arrows cycle the legal choices
and Enter confirms the selected piece.
The Players controls choose Human, CPU or Off for each colour. Keep at
least two players enabled and at least one human; New or N starts
another game with the selected modes.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
[H] opens the Hall of Fame; a human win is measured in moves, with fewer
moves ranked higher. Bring more than one piece into play so a blocked
square or capture does not leave you without a useful move.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2220.title: Mastermind
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Find the hidden code of four pegs within ten guesses. Each peg can use
one of six colours, and colours may repeat; solving the code requires
the correct colour in every position.
After a guess, ● marks a correct colour in its exact position, while ○
marks a correct colour in another position. A secret peg is counted only
once, so duplicate colours do not earn extra matches. The marks are
counts, not labels attached to particular guessed pegs.
[b]Controls[/b]
Press 1–6 or click a colour button to fill the current peg, then use
Left/Right to choose a different position. Clicking a peg selects it.
Enter, G or Guess submits the whole row; you cannot edit a submitted
guess.
N or New chooses another secret and clears the old guesses. A correct
guess wins immediately; after ten unsuccessful guesses, the secret is
revealed.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Winning games rank by guesses used, with fewer turns better. [H] opens
the Hall of Fame. Change one aspect of a guess at a time and use both
feedback counts to rule out impossible arrangements.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2230.title: Snake
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Guide the snake to food without hitting a wall or any part of its body.
Eating food grows the snake instead of removing its tail, which makes
the available corridors narrower as the run continues.
The snake keeps moving between key presses and cannot reverse directly
into its current direction. Plan turns ahead of the head rather than
waiting until it is beside a wall.
[b]Controls[/b]
Use the arrows to change direction. N or New starts a fresh run; after
game over, Enter or Space can also restart. Movement pauses while the
game window is inactive.
The field does not wrap at its edges: crossing the border ends the run.
Filling the entire board also ends it. The Info box tracks score and
level as the snake grows and the movement speed increases.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Food earns points multiplied by the current level, and higher point
totals rank first in [H] Hall of Fame. Leave a route back to open space
instead of enclosing the head inside your own body.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2240.title: Tower of Hanoi
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Move all five discs from the left tower to the right tower. Only the top
disc of a tower can move, and a larger disc may never be placed on a
smaller disc. The middle tower is temporary storage, not the winning
destination.
The order of the discs must stay largest at the bottom and smallest at
the top. An illegal move is rejected without changing the towers or
increasing the move count.
[b]Controls and history[/b]
Click a source tower and then its destination, or drag a top disc to
another tower. With the keyboard, Left/Right or 1–3 select a tower and
Enter or Space chooses the source or performs the move.
Choosing the same source again cancels that selection. U or Undo
reverses the last completed move, while N or New restores the starting
stack; the history shows the moves that remain in the current solution.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
Five discs can be solved in a minimum of 31 moves, following 2^n - 1 for
n discs. A solved game can enter [H] Hall of Fame, where fewer moves
rank higher.
Think recursively: move the four smaller discs aside, move the largest
disc towards the destination, then rebuild the smaller stack above it.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2250.title: Tron Light Cycles
content: [b]Goal and rules[/b]
Two light cycles move simultaneously and leave permanent trails. Stay
inside the arena and avoid every trail, including your own; touching the
opponent's trail or a wall causes a crash.
The surviving cycle wins. If both crash on the same tick, including a
head-on collision into the same cell, the result is a draw. A direct
reversal is rejected because it would turn into the cycle's existing
trail.
[b]Controls and pause[/b]
Player 1 uses W/A/S/D and Player 2 uses the arrow keys. Both players
steer on the same keyboard. A direction request takes effect on the next
timer tick, so the last valid turn requested before that tick is used.
P or Pause pauses and resumes the round. N or New round restarts, and
Enter can start a new round after an ending. An inactive game window or
unfocused browser pauses automatically and clears pending turns.
[b]Score and tips[/b]
A round with a winner can enter [H] Hall of Fame using its tick count
and the winning player number; higher tick totals rank first. A draw
does not submit a winning score.
Keep escape routes open and watch both heads: cutting off your opponent
is useful only if your own cycle can still get out.
[link:topic=1500]Games and Hall of Fame[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2260.title: Server Statistics
content: Server Statistics displays aggregate visits, opened content, search/link
outcomes, game activity, environment information and coarse performance
intervals. Choose a category on the left to inspect its values on the
right; category icons occupy a fixed column so labels align.
Active viewing intervals cover HELP files, documents, dialogs and games,
including DOS Prompt. Time is counted for the active target and pauses
while another window or browser tab is active.
MIDI statistics include per-track plays and active listening time,
excluding paused playback. These counters describe usage, not recordings
of what a visitor typed or an exact replay of a session.
SQLite stores aggregate counters only: no IP addresses, cookies, visitor
IDs, search text, exact timings, full referrers, raw user agents or
individual visit histories. Statistics needs a reachable server API; a
standalone browser-only copy cannot supply server-wide totals.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2270]System Information[/link]
[link:topic=1400]Search[/link]
[link:topic=2090]Dialogs and tools[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2270.title: System Information
content: System Information reports the local application's runtime, browser,
display, locale, storage and supported web capabilities. Use it when
comparing a problem between devices or checking whether the browser
offers a required feature.
Its Server section reports reachability, application version and
HELP/Docs catalog sizes. Local browser details and server availability
are separate: a browser can work while the server API is unavailable.
Refresh measures the current runtime again. Merely opening this dialog
does not submit its displayed device details to visitor statistics.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2260]Server Statistics[/link]
[link:topic=2320]DOS Prompt[/link]
[link:topic=2090]Dialogs and tools[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2280.title: Account and Login
content: Login appears at the right of the menu bar; after sign-in it becomes
your account label with Account, Configuration and Sign Out. Browsing
HELP and searching do not require an account.
[b]Profile and private C[/b]
Account edits first name, last name, nickname and validated email. The
menu prefers nickname, then first/last name; there is no separate
Display name input. If those personal fields are blank, the existing
account label is retained.
Save applies the profile, updates the menu and closes the dialog. Cancel
or closing the frame does not save profile edits. Your role is shown but
not editable here; administrators change roles in Users.
Private C shows committed overlay usage and capacity, excluding the
common DOS games and software. Profile Save preserves the login
username, Passkeys, sessions and private files.
[b]Named Passkeys[/b]
The Passkeys list can contain several authenticators. Select one and
Rename its label, or enter a name and use Add Passkey. Suggested names
describe the OS/browser, not a verified device identity; synchronised
keys may be usable on more than one device.
Adding a key requires confirmation with an existing Passkey. Renaming an
old key changes its label, not the cryptographic credential or the
account it belongs to.
Rename leaves your profile edits in place and does not save them. Use
Save to keep first/last name, nickname or email changes, or Cancel to
discard them. Refreshing the key list does not clear those fields.
[b]Optional password[/b]
Enter a new password twice, using 15–128 characters; Alt-P focuses New
password. Prefer a long, unique passphrase, because basic predictable
choices are rejected. Passwords are optional, stored as salted hashes
and rate limited.
Setting a password requires existing Passkey confirmation and signs out
other sessions, not the current one. Security actions save independently
of profile Save/Cancel, so cancelling profile edits does not undo a
completed key or password operation.
[b]Signing in and local development[/b]
Enter your email or original login username, then use Sign In for a
Passkey prompt or Password when password login is enabled. A changed
email can be used for login, but the address is not verified by an email
confirmation workflow.
Passkeys belong to a hostname: a production credential cannot
authenticate localhost. Use a browser with WebAuthn support. Explicit
local Docker development mode signs in automatically as Admin, with
separate development accounts and sessions, and must never be exposed
publicly.
Sign Out revokes the current session. While development auto-login
remains enabled, reloading or checking the local session signs in again.
Ordinary users may edit colours, but server configuration, registration
tokens and DOS/MIDI rebuilds require administrator privileges.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2290]Register[/link]
[link:topic=2040]Colors[/link]
[link:topic=2310]Configuration[/link]
[link:topic=2300]Registration Token[/link]
[link:topic=2350]Users[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2290.title: Registration
content: Open Login > Register and enter first/last name, nickname, a validated
email and a registration token in XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX form.
You then approve creation of your own Passkey in the browser.
The suggested Passkey name describes your system and browser; edit it if
another name will be clearer in your account's key list. Storing the key
in an authenticator is one step of registration, not proof that the
server accepted the account.
[b]Tokens and invitations[/b]
A token is single-use and expires after one hour. An administrator
creates ordinary tokens; on a server with no accounts, a temporary
first-administrator token appears in the server/Docker startup log.
For an administrator-created account, use its bound invitation with the
prepared email. The user enrolls the Passkey in their own browser, while
the administrator's existing session remains signed in.
[b]Confirming success[/b]
Wait for the server's success MessageBox. OK closes both Registration
and Login; if an error remains instead, read it before assuming
registration succeeded. Keep tokens private and do not put them into a
shared URL.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2300]Registration tokens[/link]
[link:topic=2350]Users[/link]
[link:topic=2280]Account and configuration[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2300.title: Registration Token
content: Administrators open Configuration > Registration Token to generate
invitations for new registrations. Generate creates a single-use token
valid for one hour; the lower list shows tokens that are still unused
and unexpired together with their expiry.
[b]Copying and revoking[/b]
Select a list row to enable Copy to Clipboard and Delete. Copy is also
available immediately after Generate and copies only the token value,
not its label or expiry. If the browser refuses clipboard access, the
input is selected for manual Ctrl+C or Cmd+C.
Delete asks for confirmation before revoking the selected token. Cancel,
Escape or closing the confirmation leaves it valid, so dismissing a
MessageBox is never permission to delete.
New token values remain readable after another sign-in because the
server stores them encrypted. Used and expired tokens are no longer
listed. Share a token privately with its intended recipient, not in a
public link or screenshot.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2290]Registration[/link]
[link:topic=2350]Users[/link]
[link:topic=2280]Account and configuration[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2310.title: Server Configuration and Rebuild
content: Server Configuration edits the default private DOS quota, backup
retention and cache lifetime. Package and maintenance actions occupy two
rows of buttons; Save/Cancel are at the bottom right, with status above
them. Host names, paths and source manifests are read-only here and are
configured on the server.
[b]Private disk capacity[/b]
An administrator can set individual user quotas in Users; a blank value
inherits the server default, initially 64 MiB. The allowed per-user
range is 1–256 MiB, and the common C drive's installed software does not
count towards the private overlay.
Reducing capacity does not delete existing saved files. Restart DOS to
reload its allowance; Users also manages roles and enabled accounts
without granting ordinary users access to server maintenance.
[b]Backup retention[/b]
Retained backups per type accepts 1–100 copies, default 2. HELP, DOS and
MIDI maintain separate recovery limits under var/backups/help, dos and
midi; DOS includes both rebuilds and package changes.
Successful jobs rotate older managed copies. A lower limit takes effect
after the next successful job, not while saving settings, and failed or
partial rebuilds retain recovery copies. Cleanup errors are logged;
migration archives and private disk revisions are outside this rotation.
[b]Cache lifetime[/b]
Cache lifetime accepts 1–3650 days, default 30, measured from successful
download or use rather than passive scans. Idle startup/hourly sweeps
expire old raw HELP/DOS/MIDI downloads and original HELP/licence files
in var/sources.
Transfers, extraction and conversion defer cleanup. Accepted
ingestion/reuse and successful server conversion refresh source age; old
file dates otherwise remain in effect. A shorter lifetime applies at the
next sweep, and still-needed downloadable archives can be fetched again.
[b]Clear cache[/b]
Clear cache requires confirmation and removes raw downloads plus all
original HELP/licence inputs in the configured sources directory,
including extracted or manually supplied files that are no longer
available online. Back up irreplaceable originals before using it.
Automatic expiry removes only old files, while manual Clear cache
removes all selected cache inputs regardless of age. Cancel, Escape or [
] makes no deletion; wait for downloads and processing to finish first.
A result reports removed file count and source size.
Published HELP, installed DOS/MIDI content, music and covers, search
indexes, accounts, private files and backups are preserved.
Uninstall/rebuild also retain original HELP inputs; confirmed Clear
cache is a separate removal action.
[b]Packages and storage[/b]
Configuration groups HELP Packages, DOS Packages, MIDI Sources and
appearance settings. Each package chooser retains its own draft; Apply
installs checked content and removes unchecked installed editions or
optional packages of that type. Closing choices before Apply saves
nothing.
Fresh servers open HELP Packages after administrator sign-in. Arrows,
Page Up/Down, the mouse wheel and shared scrollbars move long checkbox
panes; HELP versions can be chosen independently of the corresponding
compiler or DOS installation.
Published HELP lives in data/helps and Docs in data/docs. Original HELP
inputs use var/sources, archives use var/downloads/help, dos and midi,
the generated common C drive is var/dos/c, and downloaded MIDI uses
var/midi. Private DOS overlays and media in data/dos/users/<account-id>
are permanent, not cache.
[b]Rebuild DOS and MIDI[/b]
Rebuild DOS C and Rebuild MIDI open confirmation and progress directly
from the administrator's Configuration menu. Hide only hides progress;
the server continues, and selecting the rebuild again shows the same
job.
DOS rebuild recreates the common base from dos-prompt.json, keeping
private overlays and cached archives. The current browser's DOS window
is saved and closed first; restart DOS in other open tabs afterwards.
MIDI rebuild stops the old downloader, replaces generated
tracks/covers/catalog with a recoverable backup, and downloads only the
selected providers and albums from midi-sources.json.
Package changes stage shared C and record exact ownership; a failed
publication restores it. HELP conversion validates before publication,
successful editions remain available if another edition fails, and
failures retain recoverable copies for inspection or explicit Retry.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2311]HELP Packages[/link]
[link:topic=2312]DOS Packages[/link]
[link:topic=2315]MIDI Sources[/link]
[link:topic=2320]DOS Prompt[/link]
[link:topic=2060]MIDI Player[/link]
[link:topic=2350]Users[/link]
[link:topic=2316]Downloads[/link]
[link:topic=2280]Account and configuration[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2311.title: HELP Packages
content: HELP Packages installs and removes the server's published HELP editions.
It is separate from DOS Packages and MIDI Sources, though all three use
the same kind of chooser; changing a HELP selection does not change DOS
or MIDI settings.
[b]Groups, versions and selection[/b]
Choose a product group on the left, as in Help Files, then select
individual versions or guides on the right. The Description box explains
the highlighted edition. Releases are independent: removing one must not
uninstall all versions of the product.
Click or Space toggles [X], while arrows move without toggling. * marks
an edition with real published HELP, not merely a remembered request.
The pane's standard palette fills empty rows as well as the items.
Select / Deselect All below the right pane affects only the current
group. The bottom Select All / Deselect All buttons span every HELP
group; switching groups or windows keeps your unsaved draft and leaves
this dialog open.
[b]Apply and progress[/b]
Apply directly starts installation/uninstallation for the HELP selection
and opens the shared Downloads progress dialog. HELP and DOS tasks run
independently; one type need not finish before the other starts.
Downloads > More reveals unfinished editions, with actual phase names
and known percentages. New/cached archive counts and downloaded MiB
appear below the progress summary; errors use a MessageBox rather than a
status row in this chooser.
A completed transfer is not an installation receipt: an edition must
convert, validate and publish. Each successful edition appears in Help
Files immediately, and the menu refreshes while other work continues. A
later failure leaves those successful editions installed.
[b]Failure, restart and removal[/b]
Queued or interrupted jobs resume after restart, while terminal failures
require Retry. Reopening after a failure checks published HELP instead
of treating the failed saved request as installed; during a running job,
its requested target remains visible.
archive_members in the manifest selects the files to extract and
process. Unselected originals and required archive licence notices are
retained. Empty selection removes listed published HELP, not source
inputs or raw downloads.
Close before Apply saves nothing. Hide on the progress dialog only hides
it without cancelling work; caches, original HELP, private DOS files and
recoverable backups remain.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2312]DOS Packages[/link]
[link:topic=1200]HELP files[/link]
[link:topic=2316]Downloads[/link]
[link:topic=2310]Server Configuration[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2312.title: DOS Packages
content: DOS Packages manages software on the common DOS C drive; it does not
install native programs on your actual computer. The chooser shares its
layout with HELP and MIDI but keeps its own selections, and Apply
changes only DOS packages.
[b]Categories and package information[/b]
Choose a category on the left to see its package checkboxes on the
right. Icons distinguish games, programming, editors, file managers,
archive tools, graphics, sound and antivirus; the Description box
follows the highlighted package.
Language flags are aligned after the short package names and scroll with
the row. A globe means mixed or unverified language, not a guessed
country; Quadrax is Slovak. Volkov Commander is supplied without its
sources.
[b]Selecting and applying[/b]
Click or Space toggles [X]; arrows move without toggling, and the wheel
or shared scrollbars expose a long list. * indicates an installed
package verified by its disk receipt rather than an earlier saved
request.
Select / Deselect All below Packages affects only the current category.
The bottom Select All / Deselect All buttons span every DOS category;
switching categories or windows keeps all drafts and leaves the chooser
open.
UTILS and Volkov Commander are required and cannot be unchecked.
Deselect All clears optional packages only, including through the API,
and an otherwise empty selection keeps the required tools.
Required packages lead the shared download/preparation queue. Before DOS
starts, their receipts and owned files must be present; missing tools
are installed automatically. Other selected software is not implicitly
installed just by opening DOS Prompt.
The common software library has no overall size/file-count quota. Only
private user data has capacity quotas; archive safety checks stay. A
package is installed only after the disk and its receipts are live.
Staged files are not installed content, and rollback keeps them visible
as Not completed. Updating DOS C is not first-time initialization.
Apply installs checked packages and uninstalls unchecked optional ones
across the DOS draft. It is disabled only during loading/submission or
invalid settings; during an existing DOS operation it opens Downloads
without duplicating the request. Further draft edits remain for a later
Apply.
[b]Progress and private data[/b]
HELP conversion does not block a new DOS task. Its packages appear in
Downloads immediately and can transfer from independent sources while
HELP continues. The shared dialog reports download, extraction and
installation; errors use MessageBox. Closing choices before Apply saves
nothing, and hiding progress does not cancel work.
If one package stops a DOS transaction, Retry continues the saved
selected additions, including later packages marked Not started. It
retains installed software; use Apply for intended removals. Cached
archives are reused and old errors clear after successful installation.
The current DOS window saves and closes before package changes; restart
DOS in other tabs afterwards. The common drive changes, but private
overlays, media, original sources, raw caches and recovery copies are
retained. A failed HELP task is not retried by applying DOS changes.
[b]Available software[/b]
Programming includes ready-to-run Borland Museum compilers, Open Watcom
C/C++ and Fortran, Free Pascal, FreeBASIC, NASM, JWasm and DJGPP with
RHIDE. Run START where provided to enter the package's environment.
Office includes Word 5.5, As-Easy-As, Ability Plus and original
VisiCalc; tools include DOS Navigator 2, DOSZip, TDE, BIEW, GrafX2 and
DOSMid. Czech packages include Vlak, DOS Manazer, Text602, Calc602 and
Manager602. TYPE C:\SOFTWARE.TXT lists installed software and launch
commands.
Games include Cannon Fodder 1/2, the six DOS Commander Keen episodes and
Keen Dreams, Catacomb variants, Winter/Summer Challenge and Lotus, plus
shareware Duke Nukum, Duke Nukem II, Crystal Caves and Bio Menace. Newly
added optional packages stay unchecked until selected and applied.
UTILS collects ZIP/UnZip, UnRAR, UnARJ, ARJ, 7-Zip and other archive
tools with their required licence notices and available sources.
Original software licences still apply; for example, the supplied
VisiCalc is restricted to personal, non-commercial use.
[b]Installation and troubleshooting[/b]
Sources are validated and extracted before their content is cached and
installed. Configured alternatives can have different archive layouts;
optional post-install BAT scripts run once in isolated server DOSBox.
Norton Commander 4.0 is prepared from original English media without
running INSTALL.
HTTP 429 is the upstream site's rate limit, not an installed-package
receipt. Progress shows the wait/retry; a pure uninstall does not
download, though another selected category may still need installation.
Historical antivirus software retains its original licence, and an
evaluation version is not freeware. Old antivirus definitions do not
protect your modern host computer; these packages are for use inside
DOS.
[b]Related topics[/b]
[link:topic=2311]HELP Packages[/link]
[link:topic=2320]DOS Prompt[/link]
[link:topic=2316]Downloads[/link]
[link:topic=2310]Server Configuration[/link]
[link:topic=1000]Help Contents[/link]

2315.title: MIDI Sources
content: MIDI Sources selects the server's music providers and soundtrack albums.
It is separate from HELP Packages and DOS Packages, although all three
share the chooser layout; switching windows preserves each dialog's
draft.
[b]Providers and albums[/b]
The left list chooses a provider and Enable source includes it. The
right pane selects that provider's game soundtrack albums; Space toggles
an album, and switching providers keeps every unsaved choice.
The checkbox below Albums affects only the current provider's albums.
Bottom Select All / Deselect All spans every source and album, including
whether providers are enabled. Selecting all also includes future
albums; toggling a particular album switches to an explicit selection.
[b]Load albums and Apply[/b]
Load albums indexes an unindexed source and shows progress without
enabling it or downloading its music. Hide does not cancel that server
operation, and a failed catalog index can be retried.
Apply saves source and album selections directly and stops local
playback. Closing choices before Apply saves nothing; an empty selection
disables every provider instead of falling back to the entire catalog.
Selections persist in data/midi-settings.json, while provider URLs and
extraction rules stay in midi-sources.json. The previous downloader
finishes its in-flight write before processing the new selection,
retaining cached tracks, covers and index rows.
[b]Disabled content and rebuild[/b]
Unselected sources or albums leave the playlist and download queue;
their track/cover links and priority requests are disabled. Selecting
them again reuses their cache rather than requiring a separate manual
import.
Rebuild MIDI uses the same selection but replaces generated content with
a recoverable backup. Progress and errors use the shared dialogs;
ordinary members cannot change server sources.

2316.title: Downloads
content: [b]Shared processing queue[/b]
Use the indicator beside your account and clock to open Downloads, the
shared queue for HELP packages, DOS software and MIDI. It follows each
item from downloading through extraction, conversion and validation to
publication; a finished transfer alone does not mean installation is
complete.
Archive paths, sizes and links are checked before installation. New raw
downloads enter the cache only after their processor accepts them, so
rejected content cannot replace published HELP or private user data.
[b]Installing HELP and DOS packages[/b]
HELP and DOS jobs run independently, even after restart. A DOS transfer
can start while HELP converts or publishes, and HELP can start during
DOS installation. Requests for the same content type retain their order;
changing type does not replace the other's selection or progress.
Each ready HELP edition converts and publishes independently. Successful
editions appear in Help Files immediately, and a later failure does not
remove them. Conversion occupies 35–95% of an edition's gauge;
validation and publication must finish before it reaches 100%.
Each DOS change prepares one temporary C generation. A package stays
visible as Awaiting publication until the disk and receipts are live. If
publication fails, unpublished packages remain Not completed. Startup
rechecks old completion rows against published files.
[b]Restart and recovery[/b]
The shared journal in data/jobs.sqlite3 retains requests, queue entries,
phases and output checkpoints. After restart, queued or interrupted jobs
resume at verified artifact boundaries, skipping completed units only
when their output files still pass validation.
An unfinished transfer, extraction or edition is repeated safely; this
does not promise byte-range continuation of a partly downloaded file.
Terminal failures still require Retry or Apply, and removed failures
stay removed.
The global index uses the same journal and its own SQLite checkpoints.
It resumes committed, unchanged files after HELP processing releases it,
rather than rebuilding the same content from the beginning.
[b]Phase symbols and percentages[/b]
↓ means downloading, ▣ extracting and ⚙ converting, installing,
validating or publishing. Concurrent stages appear together; a known
phase total adds a percentage, while an unknown total shows only its
symbol. Waiting or discovery uses …, and changing phase clears its old
percentage.
ZIP and unar count extracted entries, 7-Zip supplies its native
progress, and HELP conversion counts source files or groups rather than
guessing time remaining. Single-track transfers and DOS installation
retain their partial progress.
The counter gives each package or album equal weight, not each provider
attempt. Source discovery can change the known amount of work; one HTML
page or archive is not the size of the whole HELP check. Installed DOS
packages are not new work, and failed checks do not count as 100%.
✓ appears only after successful processing and publication. A new batch
or retry clears the tick and starts fresh progress; partial or failed
queues keep their real progress instead of automatically showing 100%.
[b]Menus and the Downloads window[/b]
The first submenu, Completed downloads, retains successful rows at 100%.
It has its own scrollbar, independent of the main queue, whose waiting,
running and failed rows scroll when they exceed the desktop height.
Show Downloads and Package Apply open the same nonmodal progress dialog.
Its status and full filename wrap on separate rows; More/Less reveals a
green TVListBox of unfinished work, using the same row palette as MIDI
Player. Long names remain complete and can be scrolled horizontally.
Completed rows leave this details list but stay in Completed downloads.
Hide is on the left and More/Less on the right; an empty list collapses.
The compact window retains button shadows after resizing and remains
available when processing finishes.
Hide, [ ] or closing the menu does not cancel server work. Only
administrators see HELP and DOS package entries; MIDI progress is
public. The persisted queue is an operation journal, not an archive of
every download ever made.
[b]Parallel transfers and priority MIDI[/b]
Three regular workers can transfer from different sources at the same
time. Pending HELP inputs are examined for another source before filling
preparation slots with more work for a busy site. Each site and its
subdomains still share one transfer slot, including playback requests;
HTTP 429 cooldowns pause that source rather than unrelated downloads.
Music requested for playback gets a named row at the front and can use a
separate urgent worker during HELP or DOS transfers. Newer waiting songs
go first without bypassing source limits; active transfers are not
aborted by a priority request. Ordinary MIDI requests are grouped by
source and album, not into thousands of track rows.
[b]Retry, Remove and Cancel[/b]
Click a failed or Not started row to choose Retry, Remove or Cancel. The
shared action dialog wraps the full name, error and notice; buttons wrap
on narrow screens so the explanation is not truncated.
Retry repeats failed parts only and keeps successful work. A HELP retry
targets that edition and its configured alternative sources, not the
entire selection. It waits for work of the same content type, but an
unrelated HELP or DOS job need not finish first. Generic preparation
errors and deselected content cannot be retried here; an unavailable
source can still fail again.
DOS Retry continues all saved selected additions blocked by the failed
disk transaction, keeping already installed packages. Use Apply for
pending removals. Stale rows for unselected DOS packages are discarded
without deleting their files or private data. The DOS button says Retry
all and explains this scope before starting.
Remove clears only the queue entry, keeping cached, installed and
private files as well as selections. Cancel, Escape or closing [ ] makes
no change. Known MIDI failures are not retried automatically after
restart; a new playback request or applying MIDI selection can retry
them.
[b]Source checks and alternatives[/b]
Exact edition recipes run before broad family scans, and repeated source
plans are skipped within a job, including empty or failed attempts.
Discovery stops when all required originals pass their CRC checks;
filenames alone are not proof of a complete registered edition.
An unreadable download cache is fetched again before extraction. Failed
recovery preserves existing files and private data; source warnings
remain diagnostic when an edition can still recover successfully.
Unsupported Method on a RAR can mean a missing server decoder, not a
damaged download. Docker needs the 7zip-rar package as well as 7zip;
updating these dependencies requires rebuilding the image before Retry.
After bounded HTTP 429 retries, HELP defers that site for the current
operation while other sources remain eligible. A new explicit retry
starts fresh. Unsafe URLs, private peers and forbidden redirects abort
the operation rather than weakening download checks.

2320.title: DOS Prompt
content: Open DOS Prompt from the system menu. A shared TVWindow contains the
DOSBox screen. Text programs and graphics games can run inside it.
[b]Preparing the DOS environment[/b]
The first start checks the shared C drive from dos-prompt.json.
Sources marked required are installed automatically if their receipt or
owned files are missing, even on an already initialized empty disk.
jsDOS starts only after required preparation succeeds; a failure leaves
the emulator stopped and reports the error. Optional saved selections
are not installed just by opening DOS Prompt.
Initialization progress shows downloads/extraction. Later starts use the
existing base. Web Workers are required; unsupported browsers show an
error instead of downloading the whole C drive as a ZIP. Root and
package files recipes use path with text or Base64 bytes. AUTOEXEC.BAT
is an ordinary entry in root files. Changed optional recipes need
explicit installation or Rebuild DOS C. Downloads use public HTTPS;
archive hashes/sizes are not in the manifest.
Updating DOS C means an administrator is changing installed packages. It
is not a fresh disk initialization. Wait for publication to finish. The
common library has no capacity quota; private data quotas remain.
[b]Private files and cloud saving[/b]
Files are read on demand in compressed 64 KiB chunks. A signed-in user
has a private overlay: changes/deletions never modify shared C. Save C
to cloud, autosave, normal Close, Restart and EXIT save changes. Guests
have temporary disks. Never rely on a forced browser close to save your
last changes. User overlays default to 64 MiB.
The numeric keypad sends distinct DOS keys: 0-9, decimal/comma, +, -, *,
/ and Enter. NumLock controls their DOS interpretation. Keypad = uses
the regular equals key because this backend has no separate
keypad-equals code. Held keys are released when DOS loses focus.
│ Shortcut         │ DOS Prompt action                          │
│ Alt-Enter        │ Native browser fullscreen / leave it       │
│ Alt-Pause        │ Pause / resume (Alt-F16 on classic Mac)    │
│ Ctrl-Alt-R       │ Confirm restart (THelpViewer extension)    │
│ Ctrl-Alt-M       │ Leave fullscreen and open DOS Prompt menu  │
[b]Window controls and fullscreen[/b]
Zoom 2x enlarges the client area within the desktop; Zoom back restores
geometry. Fullscreen shows only the aspect-correct canvas. Inactive
windows/hidden tabs pause emulation. Keyboard input goes to DOS,
including F1; use the DOS Prompt menu for this context help.
Changing a DOS video mode adjusts the frame height to the screen ratio.
The width is kept unless the taller window cannot fit the desktop.
Fullscreen stays fullscreen; the frame adapts after leaving it.
At unchanged resolution, normal redraws do not undo manual resizing.
Dragging the resize corner keeps the DOS client in the current video
mode's width/height ratio. The frame is counted separately;
character-row rounding can leave less than one extra row. Drag
horizontally or vertically to scale both dimensions, bounded by the
desktop. HELP and document windows still resize freely.
[b]Media and host safety[/b]
Mount CD/Floppy accepts approved uploaded ISO/IMG images. Native DOS
MOUNT, IMGMOUNT and BOOT are blocked by secure mode; no host mounts.
[b]Sound and troubleshooting[/b]
Audio needs browser permission/a user gesture and correct game setup.
DOSBox defaults to BLASTER=A220 I7 D1 H5 T6. In DOOM use SETUP to enable
Sound Blaster sound/music if its source configuration is mute. Workspace
URLs keep window geometry/pause, not RAM or private media.

2340.title: Grid Viewer
content: Grid Viewer demonstrates TVGridView, a read-only list with rows and
columns. Use the arrow keys or click a cell to change selection; shared
horizontal and vertical scrollbars expose content that does not fit.
Hide headers toggles the column titles without changing the underlying
rows. A grid is useful when a plain list cannot clearly separate several
values associated with one item.
The sample rows describe Turbo Vision inheritance. This tool does not
edit application objects, save a spreadsheet or change server settings;
it exercises the common grid's selection, headers and scrolling.

2350.title: Users
content: Administrators open Users from their Configuration menu or Server
Configuration. This tool edits first/last name, nickname, validated
email, role, enabled state and private DOS capacity; ordinary members
cannot access it.
Names are optional, and existing account labels and login IDs are kept.
Legacy accounts may retain a blank email, while a supplied address must
pass the shared email validator.
[b]Add User and invitation[/b]
Add User opens the shared registration-profile form for first name, last
name, nickname and email. Create makes a member account without
enrolling a Passkey on the administrator's device, and the administrator
stays signed in.
Copy the one-hour invitation and give it privately to that user. They
finish Login > Register in their own browser with their own Passkey; the
invitation is single-use and bound to the prepared account/email.
Done clears the displayed invitation. Cancel before Create writes
nothing, but closing a completed invitation does not undo an account
that has already been created.
[b]Private C capacity[/b]
The capacity input accepts digits only, with a range of 1–256 MiB; blank
inherits the server default, initially 64 MiB. Usage counts the
committed private overlay, not common games or backup revisions.
Save applies changes immediately; restart DOS to reload the allowance.
Reducing quota does not delete existing saved files, and profile changes
do not replace the user's Passkeys or private disk.
[b]Roles and protection[/b]
Disabling an account revokes its sessions without deleting credentials
or files. The last active administrator cannot be disabled or made a
member, and the first registered administrator remains protected even
when others exist.
The founding administrator's name, email and private capacity can still
be edited. Accounts are not promoted automatically: changing a role is
an explicit administrative action.
